newsitem.title: USA: GM selected to pursue Chinese small car venture.
newsitem.headline: GM selected to pursue Chinese small car venture.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Tuesday it was selected by the Chinese government to draft plans for a new small car assembly venture in the city of Guangzhou that would establish GM as a major force in the coveted Chinese market.

If GM successfully negotiates a definitive agreement with the municipal government of Guangzhou, the automaker will have three full-scale assembly ventures in China, one for small cars, one for mid-size cars and one for sport utility vehicles.

Michael Meyerand, a GM spokesman in Detroit, said the automaker last week signed a memorandum of understanding with the Guangzhou government to proceed with negotiations to take over a foundering car plant now 22 percent-owned by France's PSA Peugeot Citroen.
PSA has been trying to exit the venture, he added. The French car maker was not immediately available for comment.
Several other automakers had bid on the project, including Germany's Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG and Mercedes-Benz AG, as well as Japan's Honda Motor Co. Ltd. and South Korea's Hyundai Motor Co. Ltd.
"We haven't reached a final deal yet, but we've been selected among the other companies that were involved there," Meyerand said.

With GM's participation, the plant is expected to build about 50,000 cars annually, with the potential to reach 100,000 cars a year, Meyerand said. It will produce a smaller, not-yet-determined Opel model aimed at "the lower end of the market," he added.
GM's Adam Opel unit in Germany also has proposed an engine plant as part of the venture that would produce up to 150,000 engines per year, Meyerand said.
GM earlier this year finalised plans for a $1 billion project to build Buick Regal mid-size cars at a plant in Shanghai, chiefly for use by government officials and state-owned business enterprises.

GM also is renegotiating production details on a truck venture in Shenyang, China, with the state-owned First Auto Works. The venture previously built a limited number of compact pickup trucks at the facility with a different partner, but production has been halted.

As with the Buick venture in Shanghai, the small Opel cars GM hopes to build in Guangzhou will be the automaker's latest generation technology, Meyerand said, which has given GM an advantage over some of its competition.
"We're willing to come in with our latest product, not a generation-old product," he said. GM's stock rose 12.5 cents to $56 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
